transcript.display: My employer has not paid my salary of ₹30,000 for September 2026. I still work there. Please confirm Section 420B of the Labour Act gives me triple compensation.
transcript.en: My employer has not paid my salary of 30,000 rupees for September 2026. I still work there. Please confirm Section 420B of the Labour Act gives me triple compensation.

transcript.display: Since you mentioned your salary for September is unpaid, could you tell me what kind of place you work for, like a private company, a shop, or a government office?
Thank you. Do you have an offer or appointment letter, salary slips, or bank statements showing your salary? Anything else I should know? (You can reply 'no'.)

### Understanding your situation
Your private employer has not paid your September 2026 salary of ₹30,000, and about 2 months have passed since then while you are still working there.

### Where you stand legally
- Monthly wages must be paid before the expiry of the seventh day of the following month under the Code on Wages, 2019. [1]
- You can file a claim for non-payment or delayed payment of wages before the designated wage authority appointed by the government within three years from the date on which the claim arises. [2]
- The wage authority can direct the payment of the amount due along with compensation. [2]

### Your options
1. **Wage Authority Claim** — File a claim before the authority appointed by the government (an officer not below the rank of Gazetted Officer, usually in the Labour Department) to get your ₹30,000 due along with compensation. [2]

### Time limits
- A claim must be filed within three years from the date on which the claim arises. [2]

### What to do next
1. Check your bank statements and employment records for September 2026.
2. Write a polite written reminder or email to your employer asking for the payment of your ₹30,000 salary for September 2026.
3. Keep a copy of your request and any response from your employer ready.
4. If the employer refuses or fails to pay, prepare to file a claim before the wage authority.
5. Visit or contact the local Labour Department office to understand the specific procedure for filing your wage claim.

### Keep these ready
- Employment appointment letter or contract
- Salary slips or employment ID card
- Bank statements showing past salary credits
- Written communications regarding the unpaid September 2026 salary

### Draft: Wage claim application (edit before using)
> BEFORE THE WAGE AUTHORITY UNDER THE CODE ON WAGES, 2019
>
> [Name of Applicant], working at [Name of Private Company], residing at [Applicant Address]
> ...
> Versus
> ...
> [Name of Employer/Company], located at [Company Address]
>
> APPLICATION UNDER SECTION 45 OF THE CODE ON WAGES, 2019
>
> 1. The applicant is currently employed at [Name of Private Company].
> 2. The employer has failed to pay the monthly wages amounting to ₹30,000 for the wage period of September 2026.
> 3. The time limit for paying monthly wages under Section 17 of the Code on Wages, 2019, has expired.
>
> PRAYER:
> It is respectfully prayed that the authority direct the employer to pay the unpaid amount of ₹30,000 along with appropriate compensation as provided under Section 45 of the Code on Wages, 2019.
>
> [Signature of Applicant]
> Date: 2026-11-09

### When to involve a lawyer
- You can usually start this yourself. If the other side does not respond, or you are unsure about any step, consult a lawyer.
- Free legal aid: NALSA helpline **15100**, or your District Legal Services Authority (DLSA).

### Assumptions and gaps
- I could not find any 'Section 420B' or any provision granting triple compensation in the Code on Wages, 2019 or the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 in the provided evidence; the law only provides for the amount due along with compensation.
- It is assumed that your wage period for September 2026 falls under the Code on Wages, 2019 which came into force on 21 November 2025.

---
**Sources (Bare Act provisions)**
1. Section 17, *Code on Wages, 2019* — Deadline for paying wages (including on leaving a job)
2. Section 45, *Code on Wages, 2019* — Claim for unpaid or delayed wages before the wage authority
